# Crawl stats

*Report* · also written Crawl stats report

The Search Console report on Google's crawling of a site: requests, response codes, file types, purpose and host status.

**Glossary** (*Crawl Stats report*): A Search Console report, under Settings, that shows how much Google crawls a site, the responses and errors it received, the file types fetched by its crawlers and the split between discovery of new URLs and refresh of known ones.

13 claims mention it: 11 shown or said at the event (4 confirmed by Google docs, 5 consistent with Google docs, 2 nothing to verify), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Crawl Stats report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9679690?hl=en).

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C339`](../sessions/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: To debug crawl issues, Google points site owners to the Crawl Stats report in Search Console, found in the Settings page under Crawl stats. `[D1-C339, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C340`](../sessions/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Search Console's Crawl Stats report shows how much Google crawls from a site, the errors Google received, and the content types fetched by the different crawlers. `[D1-C340, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C508`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Google said soft 404s, like some other problem categories, are looked up in Search Console's page indexing report, while other crawl issues are debugged in the Crawl Stats report. `[D1-C508, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C393`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: To check whether a site has a crawl budget problem, use Search Console's crawl report (Crawl Stats), which breaks crawl requests down by response and by file type and shows crawl problems Google finds. `[D1-C393, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C443`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: To judge crawl efficiency, check Search Console's Crawl Stats report: whether total crawling has plateaued over time, and whether the average response time shows the server is fast enough or is limiting Googlebot. `[D1-C443, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C462`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Google said it knew of no plans to add crawl stats to the Search Console API, because that would be a completely new part of the API. `[D1-C462, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C463`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: A Google panelist said adding a report that is a variation of the Performance report to the Search Console API would be easier than adding crawl stats, because the Performance report is already in the API. `[D1-C463, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C492`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: John Mueller said the Crawl Stats report's split of crawling by purpose, discovery versus refresh, gives a rough view of whether discovery crawling is in a reasonable range, though measuring publish-to-first-crawl time is more accurate. `[D1-C492, stage, John Mueller, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C544`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: John Mueller said that if the Crawl Stats report shows about half of a site's crawling going to discovering new pages, that is a lot of discovery crawling, which suggests that crawling of new pages is not the problem. `[D1-C544, stage, John Mueller, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C341`](../sessions/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: Gary Illyes called the Crawl Stats report the most valuable tool for debugging crawl errors, together with server logs, which he called the real thing for those who know how to read them. `[D1-C341, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C461`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: An audience member asked whether and when crawl stats will be added to the Search Console API. `[D1-C461, stage, an audience member, Day 1]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C382`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Analysis: The stage rule of thumb (under a few thousand URLs crawl budget is unlikely to be a problem) and Google's crawl budget guide (D1-C097: sites with over a million pages that change about weekly, or over 10,000 pages that change daily) leave a middle range where a site should check Search Console's Crawl Stats report before blaming crawl budget for slow indexing. `[D1-C382, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C609`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Analysis: With a typical refresh of about 30 days and deep or soft-404-like pages recrawled only every few months, link important deep pages from strong hub pages and fix pages that look like errors; then check recrawl intervals by site depth in server logs or the Crawl Stats report. `[D3-C609, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-MON-01` **MUST** · Documented: Verify every production host in Search Console before launch (its own text names it)
- `DEV-MON-03` **SHOULD** · Documented: Watch the Page indexing report and treat its not-indexed reasons as a work list (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-MON-04` **SHOULD** · Documented: Monitor Crawl stats and server logs for verified Googlebot traffic (4 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-MON-11` **SHOULD** · Documented: Measure the time from publishing a URL to Googlebot's first crawl of it (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
